entries.title: Last Orders for D, E and F
entries.html:
Three groups walked into the night and only six teams walked out. If you slept through it, you slept through a massacre, a civil war, and one of the great acts of beautiful futility this tournament has yet produced. Settle in.

Group D — the Star-Spangled survival act

Pete's USA 🇺🇸 had already done the hard work, which is just as well, because on the final night they contrived to lose 3-2 to a Turkey side with nothing but pride to play for — and even that they cut alarmingly fine. The damage was cosmetic: USA top the group regardless, and Pete sails into the Round of 32 with the smug serenity of a man who revised three weeks early. Spare a thought, though, for Sean. His Turkey 🇹🇷 produced the performance of the round, a 3-2 demolition of the group winners, the kind of result you frame and hang in the hallway — and it counted for precisely nothing. Turkey win the battle and lose the war, finishing rock bottom on three points, eliminated by the very victory that should have saved them. Football's cruellest party trick. Meanwhile Geo's Australia 🇦🇺 did what Australia do — grimaced their way to a 0-0 against Paraguay that nobody enjoyed but everybody on Geo's side will take, sneaking second on goal difference. And Barney's Paraguay 🇵🇾 are left to the indignity of the third-place lottery: four points, a minus goal difference, and a long, sweaty wait by the phone to learn whether they're one of the eight luckiest losers.

Group E — Logan versus Logan

In a development that no draft should ever permit, Logan owns both Germany and Ecuador, and on the final night they were thrown into the pit together. Ecuador 🇪🇨 beat Germany 🇩🇪 2-1 — Logan, congratulations, and also, commiserations. The twist of the knife: the win still wasn't enough to drag Ecuador into the top two, while Germany qualified top anyway, meaning Logan's blue half mugged his own black-red-gold half for sport and bragging rights alone. Sliding in behind them, quietly and ruthlessly as ever, came Joe's Ivory Coast 🇨🇮, a 2-0 win over Curaçao sealing second with no fuss whatsoever. And Curaçao 🇨🇼? Barney's lowest seed shipped seven to Germany on opening night, never recovered, and bow out bottom — the tournament's designated piñata.

Group F — Joe's Dutch masterpiece and Tunisian tragedy

Nobody had a stranger night than Joe, who owns three of this group's four teams and watched them finish 1st, 3rd and 4th. The Netherlands 🇳🇱 were imperious, a 3-1 dismantling of Tunisia capping a seven-point group win — Joe's crown jewel. Logan's Japan 🇯🇵 took second with the calm of a side that has done this before. But Joe's Sweden 🇸🇪, undone by that 5-1 evisceration by the Dutch in matchday two, are left clinging to a third-place fingernail. And Joe's Tunisia 🇹🇳… played three, lost three, goal difference of minus ten, the full wooden-spoon experience. One man, the architect of both the group winner and its whipping boys. Only in this competition.

The reckoning. Six teams through, three more (Paraguay, Ecuador, Sweden — all on four points) sweating on the best-third-placed maths. Joe emerges from the night fattest of all — two qualifiers banked — but with the haunted look of a man who also owns the group's two worst teams. Logan quietly pockets two and a maybe. Pete and Geo are through and dry. And Sean is left holding the most glorious losing scorecard in the building. Sleep well; the knockouts are coming for all of you.
